paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The One who stretches out the heavens and forms the spirit of man within him (Zechariah 12:1) is the One who says, "I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples," and "I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem" (Zechariah 12:3, 9). The leaders of Judah say in their hearts that the people of Jerusalem are their strength, "for the LORD of Hosts is their God" (Zechariah 12:5). So when the whole world piles up against you, remember where the strength was: in the LORD of Hosts being their God.

Now look at the heart of it. God pours out "a spirit of grace and prayer," and they "look on Me, the One they have pierced" (Zechariah 12:10). On that day "a fountain will be opened" "to cleanse them from sin and impurity" (Zechariah 13:1). John points to this line at the cross (John 19:34-37), and Jesus quotes the striking of the Shepherd on the night He's arrested (Matthew 26:31). Friend, grace is not something we dig up ourselves. God pours it out, and God opens the fountain.

And then comes the fire, and I'm not going to pretend it's comfortable. The LORD says He will "refine them like silver and test them like gold" (Zechariah 13:9). I know about being in a hot place, and I know it doesn't feel like a favor while you're in it. But look where the passage ends: "They will call on My name, and I will answer them," and then "They are My people," and "The LORD is our God" (Zechariah 13:9).
